subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to meet today. Quick recap and immediate next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered
- Demo of Redwood inference with your 10k daily user sample
- Latency & cost targets you set: P95 < 300ms, target model cost <$0.002/token for the primary generation path
- Key quality focus: maintain extraction accuracy on short-form summaries and avoid hallucinations on facts in the product catalog

Recommended next steps
1) I’m sending a short model shortlist and rationale below — please review and tell us which tradeoffs you want to prioritize (latency vs cost vs absolute quality).
2) We’ll run a short eval on your prompt set (attached) and the sample dataset you shared. I’ve CC’d Nikhil to scope the eval runtime and deliverables.
3) If results look good, we’ll schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive next week to go over rollout options (Dedicated pool vs Hosted with routing).

Initial recommended model shortlist (high-level) — rationale and tradeoffs
- OpenLlama-13B-q4f16: Best cost/latency balance for deterministic summarization; good on short form; lowest per-token cost but slightly lower factuality on edge cases.
- Falcon-7B-Instruct-8K: Strong instruction-following and factuality for moderate latency; good compromise if you need fewer hallucinations than quantized L13B.
- Mosaic-FT-70B (float16): Highest quality and most robust on complex prompts, but higher latency and cost — recommended for fallback route for critical queries.

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.csv (your test prompts), benchmark-summary.pdf (example benchmark from a similar retail customer), Acme-demo-recording.mp4 (recording from today).

Please let me know which tradeoff you want us to prioritize — I’ll have Nikhil spin up an evaluation run as soon as you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and shortlist. A few quick clarifying Qs: 
1) For OpenLlama-13B-q4f16, do you have an estimate of P95 latency on NV6 GPUs for our average prompt length (~120 tokens)?
2) For Mosaic-FT-70B, would you recommend that as primary or only for high-sensitivity endpoints?
3) Any obvious red flags on hallucination risk with L13B on our product catalog prompts?

We’d like to prioritize lower cost for low-value conversational flows but need high fidelity for product copy generation and legal snippets — so maybe a two-tier route. Can Nikhil scope the eval to include an A/B where L13B is primary and Mosaic is fallback?

Cheers,
Jordan

Jordan.Lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Jordan — great questions, answered inline below and added proposed eval scope.

Q1) P95 latency for OpenLlama-13B-q4f16 on NV6 (120-token prompt): ~180-240ms when using Redwood continuous batching + KV cache for short sessions. That assumes 1–2 concurrent requests per user and typical batching. We’ll include P50/P95/P99 in the benchmark.

Q2) Mosaic-FT-70B: recommended as a fallback/high-sensitivity route (legal, billing copy). Primary for critical generation only if you accept higher cost (~3–4x per-token vs L13B) and slightly higher end-to-end latency.

Q3) Hallucination risk: L13B quantized has slightly higher hallucination probability on rare product SKUs — we’ve seen this with sparse factual tables. Mitigations: prefix grounding prompts, retrieval augmentation, and thresholded fallback to Mosaic for segments with high hallucination risk.

Proposed eval scope (we’ll run against the prompt-set-v1.csv you shared):
- Run 2 A/B suites:
  A) OpenLlama-13B-q4f16 (primary) vs Falcon-7B-Instruct-8K (alt) — measure latency, cost, ROUGE/BLEU-type quality on labelled summaries, and hallucination rate on 100 catalog prompts.
  B) OpenLlama-13B-q4f16 primary with Mosaic-FT-70B fallback — measure quality delta when fallback triggers, and end-to-end P95 for routed flow.
- Deliverables: benchmark-summary.pdf (detailed metrics), model outputs for 200 prompts, prompt-level failure tags, cost-per-inference estimates.
- Timeline: 3 business days to run (depending on your data access & tokens); we can accelerate if you provide a dedicated dataset S3 link.

Nikhil/Priyom: can you confirm capacity to run both suites and estimate infra cost? I’ve attached the initial benchmark template and prompt set.

Thanks —
Marissa
